solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Repudiate broadcast on dead Iranian leader

indicators.note: in a down-the-page reading of the parse, one piece placed on (after) another follows it

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for dead, as on family trees

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Iranian

parts.note: seed that is broadcast is sown, scattered by hand

explanation.surface: A news report about a deceased Iranian ruler being publicly disowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a noun about a news report; here it is the past participle meaning scattered like seed, placed 'on' (after) D and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to refuse to acknowledge or have anything more to do with someone.

clue.text: Race to get last of Armani stock

parts.note: to race is to dash, rush at speed

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word Armani

explanation.surface: A fashion shopper sprints to grab the final item of Armani stock before it sells out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' reads as shop merchandise but is the cooking sense: a broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashi is the basic Japanese soup stock made from kelp and dried bonito flakes.

clue.text: One who mocks someone who eats greedily

definitions.meaning: a person who scoffs, jeering at something
to scoff is also, informally, to gobble food

explanation.surface: Two descriptions of an unpleasant dinner companion: one who jeers and one who gobbles.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb scoff has two senses, to jeer and to eat greedily, and the person doing either fits.

clue.text: A drop of Adam's Ale?

parts.note: Adam's ale is an old jokey name for plain water; a drop here is a fall rather than a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone asking for a small sip of plain water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests a tiny quantity of drink; read it as a vertical descent, and Adam's ale (humorous for water, the first man's only drink) supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade where a river plunges over a cliff is literally water dropping.

clue.text: Take no notice of idiot little dog bites

indicators.note: the puppy closes its mouth round the other piece, so it holds that piece inside

parts.note: a pup is a young, little dog
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Advice to ignore a silly puppy that nips.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to decline or ignore it, a phrasal-verb equivalent.

clue.text: Proverb: all dogs are good eggs primarily

indicators.note: taking the first, primary letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A proverb-like claim that every dog is a good egg, a decent sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good eggs' is British slang for decent people.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional saying expressing a general truth, the same as a proverb.

clue.text: A famous state ministry informants set up

indicators.note: in a down light, something set up is raised so that it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence
rats are informers, people who tell on others

explanation.surface: A notorious government department framed by its own spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' suggests framing someone, but it turns MOD RATS upwards; MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the condition of being a celebrity, so it is literally a state of fame.

clue.text: Normal places to see female upstarts

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level
venues are places where one goes to see events

explanation.surface: Ordinary spots where one might spot ambitious women on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The feminine -E- spelling is why 'female' is in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenue is a woman newly risen to wealth or status who is seen as not belonging there.

clue.text: A song's intro kind soprano arranges

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter, here of song's

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type
S is the musical abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A soprano arranging the opening of a song in her own style.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to sort into groups or classify, which is to arrange.

clue.text: Ghastly club visited by barbers regularly

indicators.note: the club is entered by the visitors, so the regular letters go inside it

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon

indicators.note: taking every other letter of barbers, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a club frequented by barbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A, B, R from barbers; 'visited by' puts them inside MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes something gruesome and concerned with death, as ghastly does.

clue.text: Looking at very snug fits, I must be squeezed in!

indicators.note: the single letter has to be pressed into the middle of the rearranged letters
a fit is a seizure or convulsion, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A shopper inspecting very tight clothes and worrying about squeezing into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fits' looks like clothes fitting but is the anagram signal: VERY SNUG becomes SURVEYNG, and 'must be squeezed in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveying is examining or viewing something closely, so it means looking at.

clue.text: It's more fun to change bad luck

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheery claim that change is more enjoyable than misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune is ill fortune, a straightforward synonym for adverse luck.

clue.text: A buck? That's pricey by the sound of it!

indicators.note: the word for expensive is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: Someone balking that a dollar costs too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buck' suggests a dollar; it is the male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is the male of several hoofed animals such as the fallow stag.

clue.text: Immature creature researcher finally found in rock

indicators.note: the letter is found inside the rock word

parts.note: lava is molten rock that has cooled

indicators.note: taking the final letter of researcher

explanation.surface: A scientist discovering a young organism embedded in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the juvenile form of an insect before metamorphosis, so it is an immature creature.

clue.text: Misbehaving male in bar could be one

definitions.text: Misbehaving male in bar could be one

indicators.note: the letters behave badly, falling out of their order

explanation.surface: A rowdy man in a pub is probably a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the shuffled letters of MALE IN BAR, and a loutish drinker who could be one.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamebrain is a stupid person, which describes a man behaving badly in a pub.

clue.text: Very very fat shirking Republican leader is toxic

indicators.note: avoiding the letter, so it is left out

parts.note: enormous means very fat or huge

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Republican

explanation.surface: An obese politician dodging his party boss, described as poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous means poisonous, secreting venom, which is the sense of toxic.

clue.text: Widely known and bad attack I soon rout

indicators.note: the letters are set upon and broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier boasting of a planned assault that will rout the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attack' and 'rout' both feel military; 'attack' is the anagram signal for I SOON ROUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, so it combines being widely known with ill repute.

clue.text: A flash political convention with no ethics?

parts.note: a flash is a moment, MO informally
a rally is a mass political meeting

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether a brash party conference has any principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting amorally means acting without moral standards, hence with no ethics.

clue.text: Old robbers earl pushed into waterways

indicators.note: the letter is forced inside the waterways word

parts.note: rivers are natural waterways

explanation.surface: A nobleman shoved into canals by bandits.
explanation.walkthrough: Rievers were raiders on the old English–Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Rievers (reivers) were historical Border raiders who stole cattle, hence old robbers.

clue.text: Little row over drinking first of red gins?

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the letter in, as if swallowing it
turned over, so the word for a quarrel is read backwards

parts.note: a spat is a little row, a minor quarrel

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of red

explanation.surface: A minor quarrel over who is drinking the gins and red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gins' looks like drinks; here it means snares, a sense of gin from 'engine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a trap for catching game, so gins are traps.

clue.text: Embarrassed when bad actor heads to exit drunk

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a ham is an overacting performer

indicators.note: taking the first, head letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A drunken overacting player leaves the stage red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed and embarrassed both describe feeling discomfort from guilt or awkwardness.

clue.text: Fit place to eat at if short of time

indicators.note: lacking the letter, so it is dropped from the eating place

parts.note: a table is where one eats

explanation.surface: A restaurant being judged a suitable place to dine when one is in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able means being capable, and fit has that sense, as in fit for duty.

clue.text: Playing it charms no Queen fan

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan of the rock band Queen saying their music no longer appeals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the band; it means the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchist supports rule by a sovereign, so is a fan of the Queen.

clue.text: Motorways orbiting a city abroad

indicators.note: circling round, so the motorway letters surround the other piece

parts.note: two M1s, the M1 being Britain's main north–south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Ring roads circling a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; with the digit read as I, two of them give MIMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a city in Florida, so abroad from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Gets off ship to tour ruin

indicators.note: the ship goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
to end something can mean to ruin or finish it

explanation.surface: Passengers disembark to go round some ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets off' suggests leaving a boat; it is slang for thrilling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone is dated slang for exciting them, as does getting someone off.

clue.text: Snappers possibly found in river at times

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
eras are periods of time

explanation.surface: Crocodiles or snapping fish occasionally turning up in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snappers' suggests biting creatures; it means devices that take snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameras take snaps, photographs, so they are snappers by a playful reading.

clue.text: Order of fish male servant tucks into

indicators.note: the pair go inside the fish word, as someone tucks into food

parts.note: cod is a common fish
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A manservant eating a fish meal that was ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A command is an instruction or order given with authority.

clue.text: One's bitter about famous kid's writer

indicators.note: the name lies within the phrase, the phrase being wrapped about it

explanation.surface: Someone resentful about a celebrated children's author.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Nesbit was a well-known English author of children's books such as Five Children and It.

clue.text: Assistants must withhold small, incidental remarks

indicators.note: keeping the letter held within, so it goes inside

parts.note: aides are assistants

explanation.surface: Office helpers having to keep back minor comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are passing comments, remarks made in passing or off the main topic.
